112580.impact: Users can reduce apiserver CPU usage and achieve noticeably lower list call latencies in high‑bandwidth or CPU‑starved environments.

112731.problem: kubectl's code base was importing two different versions of the `github.com/russross/blackmail` (blackfriday) library, leading to duplication, potential version conflicts, and extra maintenance overhead.
112731.affected: Developers building or extending kubectl, and any kubectl users indirectly (e.g., when rendering help/man page markdown).
112731.fix: All usages of the original `github.com/russross/blackfriday` import were updated to the v2 module (`github.com/russross/blackfriday/v2`). The vendor directory now contains only the v2 version, and related imports were adjusted accordingly.
112731.impact: Eliminates duplicate dependencies, reduces binary size and build complexity, and ensures kubectl consistently uses the newer, maintained version of the markdown parser. This improves long‑term stability and eases future updates.

112732.problem: kubeadm did not validate the format of container image repositories during init/join, allowing invalid repository strings that could cause image pull failures later.
112732.affected: Anyone using kubeadm to bootstrap a cluster with custom image repositories; clusters that would have encountered pull failures due to malformed repository URLs.
112732.fix: Added repository format validation to kubeadm, rejecting malformed image repository specifications early in the workflow.
112732.impact: Users get immediate feedback on invalid image repository definitions, preventing later pull errors and improving cluster bootstrap reliability.

112741.problem: Kube-apiserver did not expose health check Service Level Indicator (SLI) metrics, so operators could not directly observe health check performance via the standard metrics endpoint.
112741.affected: Clusters running the kube-apiserver; any monitoring system that scrapes apiserver metrics.
112741.fix: Adds a new metrics endpoint `metrics/slis` on the apiserver that emits health‑check SLI metrics, making them available to Prometheus and other observability stacks.
112741.impact: Operators can now monitor apiserver health‑check latency and success rates, set alerts, and gain better insight into API availability, improving cluster reliability and troubleshooting.

112792.problem: Kubernetes admission control lacked native support for validating resources using CEL (Common Expression Language) expressions, limiting extensibility and expressive validation capabilities.
112792.affected: Clusters where admission validation is needed and administrators want to use CEL expressions; enables existing and future admission plugins to leverage CEL validation.
112792.fix: Introduced a new feature gate `CelValidatingAdmissionExtensibility` that, when enabled, activates CEL‑based expression validation for admission control, allowing admission plugins to use CEL for fine‑grained validation logic.
112792.impact: Cluster administrators and developers can now write concise, powerful validation rules using CEL without custom webhook code, improving security, reducing operational complexity, and enabling richer policy enforcement directly in the API server.

112824.problem: Before this change, the ExpandedDNSConfig feature was only alpha and required manual enabling, limiting users' ability to configure extended DNS options for pods.
112824.affected: All clusters that run containers with a runtime supporting the expanded DNS config; workloads that rely on custom DNS settings in pod specs.
112824.fix: The feature has graduated to beta and is now enabled by default in the cluster, automatically allowing pods to use the expanded DNS configuration when the underlying container runtime supports it.
112824.impact: Clusters gain richer DNS configuration capabilities without extra feature gates, simplifying pod spec authoring. Users must ensure their container runtime implements the required DNS support, otherwise pod DNS settings may be ignored or cause errors.

112838.problem: Clusters without the LegacyServiceAccountTokenNoAutoGeneration feature gate enabled continued to auto‑generate long‑lived secret‑based service account tokens, which are less secure and increase secret sprawl.
112838.affected: All clusters that create ServiceAccounts; workloads that rely on automatically created legacy secret tokens will see those tokens no longer appear by default.
112838.fix: The feature gate has been promoted to GA and is now enabled by default. Legacy secret‑based service account tokens are no longer auto‑generated unless explicitly requested, aligning the default behavior with the security‑focused design of the project.
112838.impact: Improves cluster security by eliminating unnecessary secret tokens, reduces the surface for credential leakage, and encourages workloads to use projected service account tokens (BoundServiceAccountTokenVolume). Existing workloads that relied on auto‑generated legacy tokens must be updated to request a token explicitly.

112855.problem: There were no built‑in kubelet metrics exposing how the CPU manager allocated CPUs and performed pinning, making it difficult to observe, monitor, or troubleshoot CPU manager behavior.
112855.affected: Kubernetes users who enable the CPU manager (static policy) and need visibility into CPU allocation/pinning, as well as monitoring systems that ingest kubelet metrics.
112855.fix: The change adds new kubelet metrics that report the number of CPUs allocated by the CPU manager and the pinning state of those CPUs. These metrics are exported via the existing kubelet metrics endpoint.
112855.impact: Cluster operators can now monitor CPU manager activity through standard observability stacks, verify that the feature works as expected, and use the data to size workloads or diagnose placement issues. The metrics also satisfy a requirement for GA of the CPU manager feature.

112900.problem: Kubernetes builds were using an older Go toolchain; the build process needed to be updated to a newer supported Go version.
112900.affected: All Kubernetes components and users building Kubernetes from source.
112900.fix: The build system and CI have been updated to compile Kubernetes with Go 1.19.2.
112900.impact: Provides access to Go 1.19 security patches, performance improvements, and ensures future compatibility; users building from source get the newer binaries without changes to runtime behavior.

112907.problem: The `registered_metric_total` metric only reported a single aggregate count, providing no insight into how many metrics belong to each stability level or are deprecated, making it difficult for operators to monitor metric health and deprecation status.
112907.affected: Cluster operators and monitoring tools that scrape Kubernetes metrics (e.g., Prometheus) are affected because they receive richer metric data for analysis and alerting.
112907.fix: `registered_metric_total` now includes additional label dimensions for stability level and deprecated version, so the metric reports a separate count per stability tier and per deprecated version.
112907.impact: Operators and monitoring systems can now see the distribution of registered metrics by stability and deprecation, enabling better observability, proactive deprecation handling, and more precise alerting on metric stability trends.

112939.problem: The `preemption_victims` metric used linear bucket boundaries, which can create high cardinality and poor resolution for a wide range of victim counts, making the metric less useful and potentially increasing monitoring overhead.
112939.affected: Clusters running the kube-scheduler, especially any workloads that trigger pod preemption (e.g., high‑priority pods preempting lower‑priority pods).
112939.fix: The metric definition was changed to use exponential bucket boundaries, providing finer granularity for small values and coarser buckets for large values, reducing cardinality and improving the usefulness of the metric.
112939.impact: Improved observability of scheduler preemption behavior with lower memory/CPU cost for metric collection, enabling more accurate monitoring and alerting without affecting scheduler functionality.

112945.problem: kubeadm sub-phases could not be executed with the --dry-run flag, preventing users from safely previewing actions such as node cleanup before they are applied.
112945.affected: Administrators using kubeadm to reset clusters or clean up nodes, especially when they want to test the command without applying changes.
112945.fix: Implemented dry‑run support for kubeadm sub‑phases, e.g., `kubeadm reset phase cleanup-node --dry-run`, allowing the command to run in simulation mode without making changes.
112945.impact: Operators can now verify the effects of kubeadm sub‑phase commands ahead of time, reducing the risk of accidental deletions or misconfigurations during cluster reset or node cleanup.

112961.problem: Windows pods could not use the node's network stack (host networking), limiting certain workloads and network plugin capabilities on Windows nodes.
112961.affected: Users running Windows containers that need host network access; Windows node clusters that want to enable host networking for pods.
112961.fix: Introduced alpha support for the WindowsHostNetworking feature gate, enabling hostNetwork for Windows pods when the feature is enabled.
112961.impact: Allows Windows workloads to leverage host network interfaces, simplifying networking setups and increasing compatibility with tools that require host networking on Windows nodes.

112978.problem: When the ComponentSLIs feature gate is disabled, the kube-controller-manager does not expose the /metrics/slis endpoint, preventing users from scraping health‑check SLI metrics for the controller manager.
112978.affected: Clusters running kube-controller-manager that enable the ComponentSLIs feature gate; monitoring tools that need health‑check metrics.
112978.fix: Enabling the ComponentSLIs feature gate adds a new /metrics/slis endpoint to kube-controller-manager, exposing health‑check metrics that can be scraped by monitoring systems.
112978.impact: Operators can now monitor controller‑manager health via standard Prometheus scrapes, improving observability and allowing early detection of degraded controller performance.

112980.problem: The Kubelet Device Manager was only available as an alpha/beta feature, meaning it lacked stable APIs, default enablement, and production‑grade guarantees, limiting confidence for users needing reliable device plugin support.
112980.affected: Users running device plugins through the kubelet (e.g., workloads that require exclusive access to hardware devices) who previously had to enable the feature manually or work around instability.
112980.fix: Graduated the Kubelet Device Manager to GA. The feature is now enabled by default, its API is marked stable, version skew guarantees are provided, and documentation reflects its production‑ready status.
112980.impact: Cluster operators can now rely on the device manager for device plugin workloads (e.g., GPUs, RDMA, FPGA) in production without needing feature gates. This improves stability, simplifies configuration, and encourages broader adoption of device plugins.

113005.problem: The `kubeadm join phase control-plane-prepare certs` subcommand could not be executed in dry-run mode, preventing users from previewing the certificate preparation steps without making changes.
113005.affected: Users running `kubeadm join` to add control‑plane nodes, especially those who want to test or preview the certificate preparation phase.
113005.fix: Added native dry-run support to the `kubeadm join phase control-plane-prepare certs` command, allowing it to run safely without applying any changes.
113005.impact: Operators can now validate and troubleshoot the control-plane certificate preparation step before actually joining a node, reducing risk of failed joins and improving debugging experience.

113018.problem: The CPU Manager feature in kubelet was only available as an alpha/beta feature requiring manual enablement via a feature gate, limiting its use in production environments.
113018.affected: Users running workloads that need static CPU allocation (e.g., guaranteed QoS pods) and administrators configuring kubelet CPU Manager.
113018.fix: Graduated the kubelet CPU Manager to GA, removing the feature gate requirement and making CPU pinning behavior the default stable functionality.
113018.impact: Clusters can now rely on stable, guaranteed CPU placement for workloads that need dedicated cores (e.g., high‑performance or latency‑sensitive apps) without extra configuration, simplifying deployments and improving predictability.

113026.problem: The kube-scheduler did not expose a `/metrics/slis` endpoint, so users could not scrape detailed health‑check metrics (SLIs) for the scheduler.
113026.affected: Clusters where users want to collect scheduler health‑check metrics; enables monitoring tools to scrape `/metrics/slis` when the feature gate is on.
113026.fix: When the `ComponentSLIs` feature gate is enabled, the scheduler registers the `/metrics/slis` endpoint, making SLI metrics available for scraping.
113026.impact: Operators can now monitor scheduler health and performance via standard Prometheus scrapes, improving observability and enabling alerting on scheduler SLIs.

113030.problem: When the ComponentSLIs feature gate was enabled, kubelet did not expose the `/metrics/slis` endpoint, preventing users from scraping health‑check Service Level Indicator (SLI) metrics.
113030.affected: Users who rely on kubelet health‑check metrics for observability and alerting were unable to scrape them; enabling the endpoint resolves this.
113030.fix: The change adds the `/metrics/slis` endpoint to the kubelet when the ComponentSLIs gate is enabled, making health‑check metrics available for scraping.
113030.impact: Operators can now collect and monitor kubelet health‑check SLIs (e.g., latency, error rates) via Prometheus or other scrapers, improving visibility and reliability of node health.

113057.problem: kube-proxy did not expose Service Level Indicator (SLI) metrics, so users could not scrape health‑check related metrics when the ComponentSLIs feature gate was enabled.
113057.affected: Users who enable the ComponentSLIs feature gate and rely on kube-proxy health monitoring; monitoring setups that scrape kube-proxy metrics.
113057.fix: When the ComponentSLIs feature gate is enabled, kube-proxy now serves a `/metrics/slis` endpoint that provides health‑check SLI metrics.
113057.impact: Monitoring systems (e.g., Prometheus) can now collect detailed health‑check metrics from kube-proxy, improving observability, alerting, and troubleshooting of network proxy behavior.

113146.problem: kubectl explain only supported machine-readable output formats; users could not obtain a simple plaintext representation of OpenAPI v3 schema without custom processing.
113146.affected: kubectl users who run `kubectl explain` and need a human‑readable view of resource schemas.
113146.fix: Introduces an alpha `--output plaintext` flag for `kubectl explain`, gated behind the `KUBECTL_EXPLAIN_OPENAPIV3` environment variable, to render the OpenAPI v3 schema as human‑readable plain text.
113146.impact: Makes it easier for developers and operators to read and understand resource schemas directly from the CLI, improving usability for troubleshooting and learning, while keeping the feature hidden until explicitly enabled.

113160.problem: Azure File storage users had to use an alpha/beta in-tree volume plugin or manually enable CSI migration, which was not considered stable or fully supported.
113160.affected: Users running Azure File persistent volumes via the in-tree volume plugin or who need to migrate to the Azure File CSI driver.
113160.fix: The Azure File CSI migration feature is promoted to General Availability in Kubernetes 1.26, making the migration path stable, default, and supported without feature gates.
113160.impact: Clusters can now safely and seamlessly migrate Azure File volumes to the CSI driver as a stable, default behavior, improving reliability and reducing operational overhead for Azure users.

113172.problem: The kube-apiserver tracing implementation only emitted a limited set of spans and events, making it difficult for users to get detailed observability into API requests and internal processing.
113172.affected: Anyone using apiserver tracing (e.g., observability platforms, cluster admins, developers troubleshooting API latency or security events) gains more detailed trace information.
113172.fix: Enhanced the apiserver tracing code to emit many additional spans and span events covering request handling, authentication, authorization, admission control, storage, and other phases. The new spans are integrated with the existing OpenTelemetry instrumentation.
113172.impact: Cluster operators and developers can now obtain richer trace data from the API server, enabling finer‑grained performance debugging, latency attribution, and security/audit investigations without code changes. Observability tools that consume OpenTelemetry data will see more actionable signals.

113176.problem: There was no built-in metric to tell whether the job controller had successfully removed Pod finalizers from terminated Pods after they were accounted for in a Job's status, making it hard to detect cleanup issues.
113176.affected: Users running batch Jobs who need observability of Job controller behavior, as well as cluster admins monitoring pod lifecycle health.
113176.fix: Introduces the metric `job_controller_terminated_pods_tracking_finalizer` which reports the success/failure of finalizer removal for terminated Pods managed by the Job controller.
113176.impact: Operators and monitoring systems can now track and alert on finalizer cleanup problems for Jobs, helping to prevent stale finalizers that could block pod deletion and cause resource leaks.

113217.problem: The API server tracing did not capture latency of key request processing stages such as authorization, priority and fairness, impersonation, audit, and authentication filters, limiting visibility for debugging and performance analysis.
113217.affected: Clusters using API server tracing for observability; anyone troubleshooting API latency, especially around security and request handling components.
113217.fix: Extended the apiserver tracing implementation to record and expose latency metrics for the authorization, priority-and-fairness, impersonation, audit, and authentication filter stages.
113217.impact: Operators and developers can now see detailed latency breakdowns for these critical request handling steps, enabling faster root‑cause analysis of slow API calls and better observability of security‑related processing.

113225.problem: The ability for CSI drivers to handle FSGroup ownership changes was only available as a Beta feature behind the DelegateFSGroupToCSIDriver feature gate, limiting its default use and causing extra configuration for users.
113225.affected: Users running pods that specify a securityContext.fsGroup and rely on CSI drivers that implement FSGroup delegation. Administrators no longer need to enable a beta feature gate.
113225.fix: The DelegateFSGroupToCSIDriver feature has been graduated to General Availability (GA). The feature gate is now enabled by default, allowing kubelet to delegate FSGroup changes to CSI drivers automatically without extra flags.
113225.impact: Clusters can now use CSI drivers that support FSGroup delegation out‑of‑the‑box, simplifying security context configuration for pods that require group ownership changes and improving compatibility with storage providers.

113307.problem: The Lease objects used by the APIServerIdentity feature were named with a volatile format, causing the lease name to change across API server restarts and leading to unnecessary lease churn and confusing metrics.
113307.affected: kube-apiserver processes that have the APIServerIdentity feature enabled; any tooling that watches the lease name will see a stable identifier.
113307.fix: The lease identity naming format has been updated to use a stable, persistent name, ensuring the same lease is reused for the lifetime of an API server instance.
113307.impact: Provides consistent leader election lease identities for the kube-apiserver, reducing noise in monitoring/alerts and improving stability of the election process.

113323.problem: There were no metrics exposed for the RetroactiveDefaultStorageClass feature, so administrators could not track how many PVCs were updated retroactively with a default StorageClass or detect errors during that process.
113323.affected: Clusters that have the RetroactiveDefaultStorageClass feature enabled, especially admins and tools that rely on storage provisioning metrics.
113323.fix: Added two Prometheus metrics: `retroactive_storageclass_total` (counts update attempts) and `retroactive_storageclass_errors_total` (counts errors), emitted by the controller that implements RetroactiveDefaultStorageClass.
113323.impact: Operators can now monitor the health and effectiveness of the retroactive default storageclass behavior, quickly spot failures, and assess its impact on workloads, improving observability and troubleshooting of storage provisioning.

113324.problem: Job monitoring lacked granularity: the existing job_finished_total metric did not indicate why a Job finished, and there was no metric for pod failures handled by the pod failure policy, making it hard to observe and diagnose failure reasons and policy actions.
113324.affected: Users of Jobs who rely on Prometheus metrics for monitoring job lifecycle and pod failure handling; also any tooling that consumes these metrics.
113324.fix: The Job controller now adds a `reason` label to the `job_finished_total` metric, and introduces a new metric that counts pod failures processed by the pod failure policy, labeled by the action taken (e.g., fail, retry).
113324.impact: Operators can now see why Jobs completed (success, backoff limit exceeded, etc.) and how pod failure policies are applied, enabling finer‑grained alerting, debugging, and capacity planning for batch workloads.

113329.problem: Previously, marking a StorageClass as the default only affected newly created PersistentVolumeClaims; existing PVCs without a storageClassName were left unbound, requiring manual updates.
113329.affected: Users with existing PersistentVolumeClaims that did not specify a storageClassName and rely on default storage class behavior.
113329.fix: The RetroactiveDefaultStorageClass feature is promoted to beta, enabling the storage‑class controller to retroactively bind existing PVCs that lack a storageClassName to the default StorageClass when it is set.
113329.impact: Clusters automatically apply the default StorageClass to both new and existing PVCs, simplifying storage provisioning and preventing orphaned PVCs, which improves operational reliability for workloads that rely on default storage.

113336.problem: CSIMigrationvSphere feature was promoted to GA and permanently enabled (locked to true) in Kubernetes 1.26. The vSphere CSI driver version 2.7.x does not yet support Windows workloads, XFS file system, or raw block volumes, so those capabilities become unavailable after upgrading.
113336.affected: Clusters using the vSphere CSI driver (≤ v2.7.x) with Windows workloads, XFS file system volumes, or raw block volume support.
113336.fix: The change itself makes CSIMigrationvSphere always true. Users who require Windows nodes, XFS storage, or raw block volumes must postpone upgrading to Kubernetes 1.26 until a later vSphere CSI driver release adds support for those features.
113336.impact: Clusters that rely on Windows pods, XFS-backed PersistentVolumes, or raw block volume provisioning cannot safely upgrade to v1.26, leading to potential upgrade delays and operational inconvenience.

113340.problem: Cloud-controller-manager did not expose health check metrics via a dedicated endpoint, preventing users from scraping detailed health SLI data when the ComponentSLIs feature gate is enabled.
113340.affected: Clusters running cloud-controller-manager with the ComponentSLIs feature gate enabled, particularly cloud provider integrations that rely on health monitoring.
113340.fix: When the ComponentSLIs feature gate is turned on, the cloud-controller-manager now serves a `/metrics/slis` endpoint that provides health check metrics for scraping.
113340.impact: Enables better observability and monitoring of cloud-controller-manager health, allowing operators to integrate these metrics into alerting and dashboards and improve reliability of cloud provider integrations.

113363.problem: When a Service has trafficPolicy=Local and all pods on a node are terminating, kube-proxy would stop routing traffic to that node, causing a temporary loss of service availability.
113363.affected: Clusters using Services with trafficPolicy=Local where pods are being terminated on a node, particularly those that experienced traffic blackholing during shutdown.
113363.fix: The ProxyTerminatingEndpoints feature is promoted to Beta and enabled by default. kube-proxy now includes terminating pods as valid endpoints when they are the only pods left on a node and the Service trafficPolicy is Local.
113363.impact: Service traffic remains uninterrupted during pod termination, reducing connection drops and improving reliability for workloads that rely on Local traffic routing.

113476.problem: Windows host process containers were only available behind an Alpha/Beta feature gate, limiting their use in production and requiring extra configuration.
113476.affected: Users running Windows workloads that need host‑process containers on Windows nodes.
113476.fix: The WindowsHostProcessContainers feature is promoted to Stable, removing the feature gate requirement and guaranteeing ongoing support in the core release.
113476.impact: Clusters running Windows workloads can now use host process containers in production without special flags, simplifying deployment and improving reliability for privileged Windows containers.

113491.problem: When the pod-security admission controller was set to the `warn` level, it only emitted warnings and allowed pods that violated policies. Users relying on this behavior could unintentionally run non‑compliant workloads.
113491.affected: Clusters with Pod Security admission enabled and the `warn` level configured. Workloads that previously passed with warnings will now be blocked.
113491.fix: The default action for the `warn` level is changed to behave like `enforce`; pods that violate the configured Pod Security Standards will now be rejected instead of merely warned.
113491.impact: Clusters that use the `warn` level will start rejecting non‑compliant pods, improving security posture. Administrators may need to update policies or be prepared for pod creation failures that previously succeeded with only a warning.

113511.problem: When a node was marked OutOfService, volumes attached to that node were not automatically detached, requiring manual cleanup and potentially leaving orphaned volumes.
113511.affected: Cluster operators and workloads that rely on CSI volume attachments when nodes are taken out of service, especially during node maintenance or scaling down.
113511.fix: Introduces the NodeOutOfServiceVolumeDetach feature, now graduated to beta, which automatically detaches CSI volumes from a node when it enters the OutOfService state.
113511.impact: Simplifies node decommissioning and improves storage resource hygiene, reducing manual steps and preventing orphaned volume issues for clusters using CSI drivers.

113519.problem: There were no exposed metrics for tracking when the Pod Garbage Collector force-deletes pods or encounters errors during those deletions, making it difficult for operators to monitor and alert on this behavior.
113519.affected: Cluster administrators and monitoring systems that rely on metrics from the Pod Garbage Collector; the change is relevant when pods are force-deleted due to GC constraints.
113519.fix: Adds two new Prometheus metrics—`force_delete_pods_total` (counts successful forced deletions) and `force_delete_pod_errors_total` (counts errors encountered during forced deletions)—to the Pod GC controller in kube-controller-manager.
113519.impact: Provides operators with observability into forced pod deletions, enabling better monitoring, alerting, and troubleshooting of garbage collection issues, which improves cluster reliability and debugging capabilities.

113544.problem: There were no events emitted when the TopologyAwareHints feature was turned on or off, making it hard for operators to track changes and debug scheduling behavior.
113544.affected: Clusters using the scheduler's TopologyAwareHints feature, especially administrators and monitoring systems that need visibility into hint configuration changes.
113544.fix: The scheduler now publishes Kubernetes events whenever TopologyAwareHints is enabled or disabled, providing observable signals for the change.
113544.impact: Operators and monitoring tools can now see when TopologyAwareHints is toggled, improving observability, troubleshooting, and integration with alerting pipelines.

113550.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with an older Go version, which could miss upstream security fixes, bug fixes, and performance improvements provided by newer Go releases.
113550.affected: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.) are rebuilt with Go 1.19.3.
113550.fix: The build process has been updated to use Go 1.19.3, recompiling all components with the newer compiler and standard library.
113550.impact: All Kubernetes components receive the latest Go runtime security patches and performance improvements, reducing the risk of compiler‑related bugs and ensuring compatibility with newer Go ecosystem tooling.

113596.problem: When the kubelet process restarts, it discards its cached SELinux mount contexts, causing SELinux relabeling to be lost for volumes that rely on the SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod feature.
113596.affected: Workloads that rely on SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod (pods using SELinux‑enabled volumes) on nodes where the kubelet may be restarted.
113596.fix: Implemented reconstruction of SELinux mount context after kubelet restart, completing the SELinuxMountReadWriteOncePod feature so the kubelet retains or rebuilds its SELinux context cache automatically.
113596.impact: Pods that use SELinux labeling on their volumes will no longer encounter SELinux permission errors after a kubelet restart, improving security enforcement and stability for SELinux‑enabled clusters.

113609.problem: cAdvisor was the only source for container and pod metrics; CRI implementations could not provide metrics, limiting observability and future deprecation of cAdvisor.
113609.affected: Clusters using the metrics API (e.g., metrics-server) and any node runtimes that rely on CRI; primarily affects kubelet behavior.
113609.fix: Alpha implementation in the kubelet that queries container and pod metrics via the CRI instead of cAdvisor, exposing them through the metrics API.
113609.impact: Allows metrics providers to obtain data directly from the container runtime, improves consistency across runtimes, and paves the way for eventual removal of cAdvisor.

113629.problem: There was no built‑in way to discover how many kube‑apiserver instances are running in a cluster, making HA monitoring and future features that need API server identity difficult.
113629.affected: Kubernetes control‑plane clusters, especially those running multiple API server replicas; administrators and monitoring tools that need API server identity.
113629.fix: The APIServerIdentity feature is promoted to Beta and is enabled by default. Each kube‑apiserver now creates a Lease object in the kube‑system namespace, representing its identity and liveness.
113629.impact: Cluster operators and tooling can read the Lease objects to count active API servers, improving HA observability and enabling upcoming features such as the Storage Version API that depend on knowing which API servers are alive.

113636.problem: Bash shell completion for kubectl did not provide inline descriptions of commands and flags, forcing users to look up documentation to understand their purpose.
113636.affected: All users running kubectl with Bash shell completion are affected; they will now see descriptive help in the auto‑complete suggestions.
113636.fix: The bash completion script for kubectl is updated to embed descriptive text for each command and flag, so `kubectl <TAB>` now shows helpful explanations alongside completion options.
113636.impact: Improves usability and productivity for developers and operators who rely on bash autocompletion, reducing context switches to documentation and lowering the chance of misusing flags.

113710.problem: The kubelet CLI flags `pod-eviction-timeout` and `enable-taint-manager` are deprecated and will be removed in v1.27, which can cause kubelet startup failures for clusters that still use these flags.
113710.affected: Clusters that configure kubelet with `pod-eviction-timeout` or `enable-taint-manager` flags.
113710.fix: The flags have been removed; users must stop using them and rely on the default behavior or alternative configuration options before upgrading to v1.27.
113710.impact: Administrators need to update their kubelet startup scripts and configuration to remove the deprecated flags to avoid breakage during upgrade.

113769.problem: Older cAdvisor version (pre‑v0.46.0) could miss or misreport container resource usage metrics, limiting accurate monitoring.
113769.affected: Kubelet on all nodes that report metrics; any workloads that rely on cAdvisor metrics (e.g., HorizontalPodAutoscaler, Prometheus).
113769.fix: The kubelet now bundles cAdvisor v0.46.0, which includes bug fixes, performance improvements, and updated metric collection.
113769.impact: Improved reliability of node‑level and pod‑level metrics used by dashboards, autoscalers, and monitoring tools.

113819.problem: Users had to use the alpha command `kubectl alpha events` to view cluster events, which required the alpha flag and lacked the stability and discoverability of a regular command.
113819.affected: All kubectl users who query or monitor events in a cluster, especially scripts and automation that relied on the alpha command.
113819.fix: The alpha command has been promoted to a stable, top‑level command `kubectl events`, making it part of the regular CLI without the alpha prefix.
113819.impact: Simplifies event inspection for all kubectl users, encourages broader usage, and aligns the command with the stable CLI surface, reducing confusion and improving tooling consistency.

108250.problem: kube-proxy had no way to prevent NodePort services from being bound to the loopback interface in iptables mode on IPv4, causing NodePort traffic to be reachable locally on the node.
108250.affected: Clusters running kube-proxy in iptables mode on IPv4 where NodePort services might be unintentionally reachable via 127.0.0.1 on the node.
108250.fix: Introduced a new kube-proxy flag `--iptables-localhost-nodeports` (default true). When set to false, kube-proxy stops creating iptables rules that expose NodePort services on the node's loopback addresses.
108250.impact: Administrators can now disable localhost access to NodePort services, reducing accidental local exposure and improving node‑level security posture for IPv4 clusters using iptables mode.

108501.problem: HorizontalPodAutoscaler controller processed all metrics sequentially with a single goroutine, causing large delays (e.g., 120s vs 15s) when many HPAs used custom/external metrics.
108501.affected: Clusters running large numbers of HorizontalPodAutoscaler objects, particularly those using custom or external metrics, and the workloads they control.
108501.fix: kube-controller-manager now accepts the '--concurrent-horizontal-pod-autoscaler-syncs' flag to configure multiple HPA controller workers, enabling parallel metric processing.
108501.impact: Reduces scaling latency and improves responsiveness of HPAs, especially in clusters with many HPAs or external/custom metrics, preventing scaling drifts.

109525.problem: `kubectl wait` did not honor the `--for=jsonpath=...` flag; it returned immediately instead of waiting for the specified JSON path to appear, causing scripts that relied on this behavior to fail or proceed prematurely.
109525.affected: Any user or automation that uses `kubectl wait` with the `--for=jsonpath=` flag to wait for a field to appear in a resource.
109525.fix: The `kubectl wait` implementation was updated to monitor the target JSONPath expression and block until the field becomes present (or the timeout expires).
109525.impact: Users can now reliably wait for arbitrary object fields to materialize, improving automation scripts, CI pipelines, and operational tooling that depend on `kubectl wait` for state verification.

111023.problem: Kubernetes did not have a generic way for Pods to request special resources beyond the limited Device Plugins mechanism, restricting flexibility for custom resource allocation models.
111023.affected: Pods that need custom or special resources and cluster administrators who want to expose such resources to workloads.
111023.fix: Introduced a new `ResourceClaim` API in the `resource.k8s.io/v1alpha1` group, gated by `DynamicResourceAllocation`. Pods can now create and reference ResourceClaims to request resources that may be provided at node level, cluster level, or via custom implementations.
111023.impact: Enables users and platform developers to define and claim arbitrary resources for workloads, improving resource scheduling, supporting new hardware or software resource types, and reducing reliance on the older device plugin model.

111333.problem: Previously there was no API or kubectl command for a user to retrieve their own subject attributes (e.g., groups, scopes) from the control plane, making it hard to introspect identity or debug RBAC issues.
111333.affected: All Kubernetes users and administrators who need to discover their own authentication attributes, including scripts and CI pipelines that interact with the API.
111333.fix: Introduced a new SelfSubjectReview API and the corresponding `kubectl auth whoami` command that returns the caller's subject attributes, enabling users and scripts to query their own identity information directly.
111333.impact: Provides a simple, reliable way to view the current user's attributes, aiding debugging of RBAC, improving automation scripts, and enhancing security auditing by letting users verify their effective identity without needing elevated permissions.

111616.problem: The external Credential Provider feature was only available as a beta API (v1beta1), limiting its stability guarantee and requiring users to track a beta version.
111616.affected: Users running kubelet with external credential provider plugins, and any workload that relies on those plugins for image pull or other authentication needs.
111616.fix: The feature is promoted to GA. The Credential Provider Plugin and Credential Provider Config APIs are moved from v1beta1 to the stable v1 version, without any functional changes.
111616.impact: Clusters that use the external credential provider (e.g., for pulling images from private registries) now have a stable, GA‑supported API. Existing configurations continue to work, but new deployments should reference the v1 API. This improves reliability and reduces churn for users.

112306.problem: The FlowSchemaStatus and PriorityLevelConfigurationStatus condition slices lacked the strategic merge patch annotations (patchStrategy and patchMergeKey), causing apply/patch operations to misbehave and leading to test flakiness. Additionally, the field name 'assuredConcurrencyShares' was inconsistent with the spec and required renaming.
112306.affected: Users and controllers that interact with the Priority and Fairness API (FlowSchema and PriorityLevelConfiguration), especially those using kubectl apply or strategic merge patch.
112306.fix: Introduce a new v1beta3 version of the Priority and Fairness API that (1) renames spec.limited.assuredConcurrencyShares to spec.limited.nominalConcurrencyShares, and (2) adds the required strategic merge patch annotations to the Conditions slices of FlowSchema and PriorityLevelConfiguration resources.
112306.impact: Clients can now safely use strategic merge patch and server-side apply on FlowSchema and PriorityLevelConfiguration objects without unexpected conflicts. The API becomes more consistent, and the apply reset fields test is no longer flaky, improving overall reliability of the flow-control subsystem.

112360.problem: Pods terminated during a graceful node shutdown or node pressure eviction did not have a specific failure condition, so controllers and users could not distinguish these disruptions from other pod failures, leading to unnecessary restarts or retries.
112360.affected: Pods that are terminated because of graceful node shutdowns or node pressure evictions; workloads managed by controllers such as Deployments, StatefulSets, DaemonSets, etc.
112360.fix: The kubelet now adds a new PodFailureCondition called `DisruptionTarget` to pods that are being terminated because of a graceful node shutdown or node pressure eviction.
112360.impact: Controllers (e.g., Deployments, StatefulSets) and applications can now detect that a pod termination was due to node disruption, allowing them to avoid unnecessary pod recreation and improve observability of node‑related failures.

112521.problem: The scheduler API only allowed a single global `percentageOfNodesToScore` setting, preventing different scheduler profiles from using tailored node‑scoring percentages.
112521.affected: Clusters that use multiple scheduler profiles and need different node‑scoring percentages per profile.
112521.fix: Added a `percentageOfNodesToScore` field to the SchedulerProfile spec in the v1 API. When set on a profile, it overrides the global setting for that profile.
112521.impact: Administrators can now tune the node‑scoring fraction per profile, improving scheduling latency and allowing more granular performance optimization for workloads that use different profiles.

112744.problem: StatefulSets could only start replica numbering at ordinal 0, making it difficult to migrate or integrate workloads that required a different starting index or to avoid naming collisions.
112744.affected: Users deploying or managing StatefulSets that need custom ordinal numbering, such as migration scenarios or services relying on specific pod names.
112744.fix: Introduced the optional `.spec.ordinals.start` field in the StatefulSet spec, allowing users to specify any non‑negative integer as the first replica ordinal.
112744.impact: Enables seamless migration of existing stateful workloads, custom naming schemes, and better integration with external systems that expect specific pod ordinal numbers, reducing manual work and potential errors.

112895.problem: The MixedProtocolLBService type was only available as a beta feature, requiring a feature gate and lacking guaranteed long‑term support.
112895.affected: Users who rely on or plan to use MixedProtocolLBService (service type) in their workloads, as well as clusters that need a stable load‑balancer service for mixed protocol traffic.
112895.fix: MixedProtocolLBService has been graduated to GA. The service type is now stable, no longer requires a feature gate, and is fully supported by the API server and cloud‑controller manager.
112895.impact: Clusters can now use MixedProtocolLBService in production without feature‑gate gymnastics, gaining stable behavior and guaranteed support. Existing beta usage continues to work unchanged.

112914.problem: Kubelet topology manager policies could not be fine‑tuned, and there was no way to prefer NUMA node sets that are physically closer, limiting performance optimization for NUMA‑aware workloads.
112914.affected: Users running NUMA‑aware workloads that rely on the topology manager for pod resource allocation. The change also benefits cluster operators who want more control over pod placement on multi‑NUMA nodes.
112914.fix: Introduced a new `--topology-manager-policy-options` flag in the kubelet. The first option, `prefer-closest-numa-nodes`, lets the topology manager favor sets of NUMA nodes with shorter distances when making admission decisions.
112914.impact: Allows cluster operators and workload developers to improve pod performance on NUMA hardware by reducing memory latency and improving cache locality, leading to more efficient resource usage and potentially higher throughput for latency‑sensitive applications.

113171.problem: Clusters lacked a unified discovery endpoint for aggregated API servers, requiring clients to make separate discovery calls for each aggregated API.
113171.affected: Any workload or tooling that performs API discovery, especially those interacting with aggregated API servers, when the feature gate is enabled.
113171.fix: Introduced the AggregatedDiscoveryEndpoint, an alpha‑level discovery endpoint that can be enabled via the AggregatedDiscoveryEndpoint feature gate, allowing a single discovery request to return both built‑in and aggregated API resources.
113171.impact: Clients (e.g., kubectl, client‑go) can retrieve a complete API surface with one request, simplifying client code and reducing network round‑trips. Enables early testing of aggregated discovery in clusters that enable the feature flag.

113186.problem: PVCs could only reference a data source (e.g., a VolumeSnapshot) in the same namespace, preventing users from using snapshots or other data sources across namespaces.
113186.affected: Users creating PersistentVolumeClaims that rely on a data source (such as VolumeSnapshots) located in a different namespace.
113186.fix: Introduced an optional alpha `namespace` field on the `dataSourceRef` of a PersistentVolumeClaim, allowing a PVC to specify the namespace of the referenced data source.
113186.impact: Enables cross‑namespace snapshot and other data‑source usage, paving the way for richer storage workflows and future CSI features without requiring work‑arounds.

113274.problem: Users could not control when a Pod is considered scheduling‑ready, making it difficult to delay scheduling until certain conditions (e.g., init containers, sidecars) are satisfied.
113274.affected: Workloads that need to postpone scheduling, such as Pods with init containers, sidecar injection, or custom controllers that set scheduling gates.
113274.fix: Introduces the .spec.schedulingGates field in the Pod API. Pods with pending scheduling gates are excluded from the scheduler until all gates are removed, allowing explicit control over scheduling readiness.
113274.impact: Enables workloads to reliably defer scheduling, improving coordination of multi‑container setups and custom controllers without needing work‑arounds.

113275.problem: Scheduler configuration did not provide a hook to run custom logic before a pod is enqueued, limiting plugin extensibility for pre‑enqueue processing such as validation or mutation.
113275.affected: Clusters using the kube-scheduler and custom scheduler plugins that need to run logic before pods are enqueued.
113275.fix: Introduced a new `preEnqueue` extension point in the scheduler's component config (v1beta2, v1beta3, v1), allowing scheduler plugins to execute code before a pod is placed onto the scheduling queue.
113275.impact: Enables developers to add custom pre‑enqueue checks or transformations, expanding scheduler plugin capabilities and giving clusters finer control over pod admission into the scheduling pipeline.

113314.problem: Kubernetes lacked a native, extensible way to define validating admission policies using expressive CEL expressions, limiting custom admission control capabilities.
113314.affected: Users who need custom admission validation (cluster admins, developers) and any workloads subject to new validation policies.
113314.fix: Introduces the admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1alpha1 API for ValidatingAdmissionPolicy, enabled via the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy feature gate and runtime-config, allowing administrators to write admission validation logic with CEL.
113314.impact: Cluster administrators can now implement flexible, fine‑grained admission validation rules without custom webhooks, simplifying policy management and improving security posture.

113351.problem: The EndpointSliceTerminatingCondition feature gate was previously behind a flag, requiring users to enable it manually. This caused extra configuration and potential confusion, especially as the feature was effectively stable.
113351.affected: Administrators who enabled the EndpointSliceTerminatingCondition feature gate and any workloads relying on custom endpoint termination behavior. Also affects clusters that have the flag set in component configs (kube-apiserver, controller-manager).
113351.fix: The feature gate has been graduated to GA, the flag is now locked (always enabled) and will be removed in v1.28, eliminating the need for manual gating.
113351.impact: Clusters no longer need to set the EndpointSliceTerminatingCondition flag. Existing configurations that reference the flag will need to be cleaned up before v1.28 to avoid startup errors. The GA status ensures the terminating condition on EndpointSlices is consistently available, improving reliability of service endpoint handling.

113360.problem: Jobs could not distinguish between retriable and non-retriable pod failures, causing all pod failures to be treated the same way (typically triggering a retry), which made it difficult to stop a job after a definitive failure.
113360.affected: Any workload that uses the Job API (e.g., batch processing, CI/CD pipelines, cron jobs) and needs fine‑grained control over retry behavior.
113360.fix: Introduces a beta feature that adds explicit pod failure classifications for Jobs: retriable failures (which cause the Job controller to create a replacement pod) and non‑retriable failures (which mark the Job as failed without further retries). The feature is gated and enabled by default in this release.
113360.impact: Users can now define more precise failure handling for batch workloads, preventing endless retry loops and reducing resource waste. This improves reliability and predictability of Job‑based processing pipelines.

113375.problem: When a PodDisruptionBudget (PDB) is in place, pods that are not Ready are prevented from being evicted even if they are unhealthy, which can block node drains or other maintenance operations.
113375.affected: Clusters that use PodDisruptionBudgets and need to evict pods that are not Ready, such as during node drains or upgrades.
113375.fix: Introduces an alpha field `spec.unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy` on PDBs. When the `PDBUnhealthyPodEvictionPolicy` feature gate is enabled, setting this field to `"AlwaysAllow"` permits eviction of pods without a Ready condition regardless of the PDB's overall health.
113375.impact: Operators can now safely evict unhealthy pods during maintenance without being blocked by a healthy PDB, improving node lifecycle handling and reducing disruption risk.

113485.problem: The existing metric `apiserver_flowcontrol_request_concurrency_limit` was ambiguous, representing both the configured concurrency limit and the enforced limit for API priority levels. Operators and monitoring tools could not reliably distinguish the intended value. Additionally, there was no way to configure borrowing of seats between priority levels.
113485.affected: Operators using Priority and Fairness for API request throttling and any monitoring systems that relied on the old `apiserver_flowcontrol_request_concurrency_limit` metric.
113485.fix: Introduced borrowing support for API priority levels by adding `lendablePercent` and `borrowingLimitPercent` fields under `.spec.limited`. Added a suite of new metrics (e.g., `apiserver_flowcontrol_nominal_limit_seats`, `apiserver_flowcontrol_current_limit_seats`, demand and target seat metrics) to expose configured limits, actual allocations, and demand. Clarified that the legacy metric now only reports the configured concurrency limit.
113485.impact: Cluster operators can now configure flexible seat borrowing to improve API request handling under load, and have richer observability into flow‑control behavior. Monitoring dashboards must be updated to interpret the renamed meaning of the old metric and to incorporate the new metrics for accurate capacity planning and troubleshooting.

113496.problem: The ServiceInternalTrafficPolicy field was in beta, requiring a feature gate and lacking a stable API, which prevented production use and caused uncertainty for users needing internal traffic routing control.
113496.affected: Users who configure or depend on ServiceInternalTrafficPolicy (previously in beta) and any workloads that rely on Service internal traffic routing.
113496.fix: Graduates ServiceInternalTrafficPolicy to GA, removing the feature gate, making the field stable in the core Service API, and providing default behavior and documentation for production workloads.
113496.impact: Clusters can now rely on a stable internal traffic policy for Services without extra feature‑gate configuration, enabling predictable pod‑to‑pod communication within a Service and simplifying production deployments.

113500.problem: The podTopologySpread scheduler plugin required an explicit NodeInclusionPolicy configuration, and the policy was disabled by default, forcing users to manually enable it to get node‑aware spreading behavior.
113500.affected: Any workloads that use podTopologySpread constraints (pods, Deployments, StatefulSets, etc.) because the scheduler now automatically applies the node inclusion policy.
113500.fix: NodeInclusionPolicy is now enabled by default in the podTopologySpread plugin, so the scheduler automatically applies node‑aware topology spreading without additional configuration.
113500.impact: Users of pod topology spread constraints get better default pod placement across nodes, simplifying configuration and improving workload distribution and resilience.

113510.problem: Job objects were tracked using a deprecated annotation (batch.kubernetes.io/job-tracking) and without finalizers, which could lead to unreliable cleanup and lingering Pods. Users could also remove the annotation, causing the control plane to re‑add it inconsistently.
113510.affected: Any cluster using Job resources, especially those that relied on the batch.kubernetes.io/job-tracking annotation or experienced lingering Pods after Job completion.
113510.fix: Graduated the JobTrackingWithFinalizers feature to GA. Jobs are now tracked via a controller‑added finalizer and receive the batch.kubernetes.io/job-tracking annotation only for backward compatibility. The control plane enforces the finalizer, restores the annotation if manually removed, and deprecates the annotation for new Jobs (no longer added after v1.27).
113510.impact: Provides a reliable, stable mechanism for Job lifecycle tracking, reducing leftover Pods and eliminating reliance on a deprecated annotation. Users upgrading to v1.27 will see the annotation ignored, preventing unexpected behavior.

110618.problem: The kubelet no longer supports the Container Runtime Interface (CRI) version v1alpha2, so runtimes that only implement v1alpha2 cannot be used.
110618.affected: Users running container runtimes that only support CRI v1alpha2, affecting pod startup on those nodes.
110618.fix: Support for CRI v1alpha2 has been removed; runtimes must implement the stable CRI v1 version to be compatible with the kubelet.
110618.impact: Clusters using a container runtime that only implements CRI v1alpha2 will fail to start pods until the runtime is upgraded to support CRI v1, requiring administrators to update or replace the runtime.

111096.problem: kubectl api-resources did not show the resource categories and lacked a way to filter resources by category, making it harder for users to discover and list related resources.
111096.affected: kubectl users who list API resources, especially when they need to discover or filter resources by logical categories.
111096.fix: Added a categories column to the wide output (-o wide) of kubectl api-resources and introduced a new --categories flag that filters the listed resources to those belonging to one or more specified categories.
111096.impact: Improves the usability of kubectl for operators and developers by allowing easier discovery of related resources and enabling scripts to target specific categories, reducing manual lookup effort.

111726.problem: The scheduler dumper did not provide any visibility into how many pending pods were in each of its internal scheduling queues, making it difficult for operators to diagnose scheduling delays or bottlenecks.
111726.affected: Cluster operators and developers who rely on scheduler diagnostics to understand pod scheduling backlogs.
111726.fix: The kube-scheduler dumper now includes a summary section that reports the count of pending pods for each internal queue, exposing this information via the scheduler's diagnostic endpoints.
111726.impact: Operators gain better observability into the scheduler's internal state, enabling quicker identification of scheduling pressure points and more efficient troubleshooting of pod placement issues.

111973.problem: Beta APIs that were scheduled for removal in Kubernetes v1.26 are no longer served by the API server, causing any client that still uses those removed beta versions to receive errors.
111973.affected: Any workloads, controllers, scripts, or tools that still rely on the beta API versions scheduled for removal in v1.26.
111973.fix: The API server now stops serving the deprecated beta API groups/versions that were slated for removal, enforcing migration to the corresponding stable (GA) APIs.
111973.impact: Clusters will reject requests to the removed beta APIs, which can break applications, controllers, or scripts that have not been updated. Users must update manifests, clients, or controllers to use the supported GA APIs to keep the workloads functional.

111998.problem: e2e test suites could not reliably register cleanup or setup callbacks after creating a test framework instance, and had to use the now-removed f.AddAfterEach and AddCleanupAction APIs, leading to ordering uncertainties and extra maintenance.
111998.affected: Developers writing Kubernetes e2e tests; any CI pipelines that rely on the e2e testing framework.
111998.fix: The framework now allows registration of callbacks directly with ginkgo.BeforeEach, ginkgo.AfterEach, and ginkgo.DeferCleanup immediately after framework creation. The callbacks are guaranteed to run after the framework is initialized and before it is torn down. The old f.AddAfterEach and AddCleanupAction functions have been removed in favor of ginkgo.DeferCleanup.
111998.impact: Test authors get a simpler, more predictable way to add per‑test setup and teardown logic, reducing test flakiness and maintenance overhead. The change does not affect cluster runtime behavior.

112000.problem: kubeadm passed the flag --container-runtime=remote to the kubelet during init/join/upgrade even though dockershim was removed and "remote" is the only valid value, making the flag redundant and potentially confusing.
112000.affected: Clusters provisioned or upgraded with kubeadm. Any node where kubeadm invokes the kubelet during init, join, or upgrade.
112000.fix: Removed the usage of the --container-runtime=remote flag from all kubeadm commands (init, join, upgrade). kubeadm now starts the kubelet without specifying this flag.
112000.impact: Prevents unnecessary flag warnings, reduces configuration noise, and aligns kubeadm with the current kubelet behavior where the container runtime flag is implicit. No functional change to clusters, but simplifies upgrade paths and documentation.

112008.problem: CoreDNS pods created by kubeadm include a toleration for the "node-role.kubernetes.io/master" taint even though, starting with kubeadm v1.25, control‑plane nodes no longer receive that taint. The unnecessary toleration adds noise to manifests and may cause confusion for users customizing addon deployments.
112008.affected: Clusters provisioned with kubeadm that use the default CoreDNS addon, and any users who have copied the CoreDNS manifest into their own addon manifests.
112008.fix: The CoreDNS deployment generated by kubeadm now omits the toleration for the "node-role.kubernetes.io/master" taint. Users can also manually remove this toleration from any custom addon manifests they manage.
112008.impact: Manifests become cleaner and easier to understand. There is no functional change to CoreDNS scheduling, but removing the stale toleration avoids potential misunderstanding and aligns manifests with the current taint behavior on control‑plane nodes.

112015.problem: The in-tree GlusterFS storage driver, which had been deprecated in v1.25, has been removed in v1.26. Clusters that still rely on the in-tree driver will fail to attach or provision volumes after upgrading.
112015.affected: Clusters upgrading to Kubernetes v1.26 that still have GlusterFS in-tree volume plugins enabled or existing PVs/PVCs that reference the in-tree driver.
112015.fix: The driver code has been deleted from the core Kubernetes codebase. Users must migrate to the external GlusterFS CSI driver (or another compatible storage solution) before upgrading to v1.26.
112015.impact: Without migration, workloads that use GlusterFS PersistentVolumes or StorageClasses will experience volume provisioning/attachment failures, leading to pod startup failures. Migration to CSI restores storage functionality.

112043.problem: The core e2e test framework was monolithic, and optional features like resource monitoring and metrics were always compiled in, causing larger binary size and compilation issues for test suites that only needed core functionality.
112043.affected: Developers of e2e test suites and CI pipelines that compile the Kubernetes test framework.
112043.fix: Refactored test/e2e/framework to keep only essential core code. Optional capabilities (resource monitoring, log size monitoring, metrics gathering, debug dumps) are now provided as separate init packages that test suites can import explicitly. A migration script is supplied to update existing code that relied on the previous unified imports.
112043.impact: Reduces e2e test binary size and compile time, and makes the framework more modular. Developers with existing e2e tests may need to adjust imports, but a provided script can automatically fix most compile errors.

112058.problem: The cluster's bundled cri-tools version was outdated, missing recent bug fixes, compatibility improvements, and new features needed for up‑to‑date CRI debugging.
112058.affected: Users who run `crictl` or rely on cri-tools for debugging containers; any workflow that uses CRI tooling in CI/CD or troubleshooting.
112058.fix: Update the bundled cri-tools package to v1.25.0, bringing in the latest upstream changes.
112058.impact: Cluster administrators and developers get an up‑to‑date `crictl` CLI with improved stability, bug fixes, and support for newer container runtimes, reducing troubleshooting friction.

112076.problem: In Kubernetes 1.25, when the LocalStorageCapacityIsolationFSQuotaMonitoring feature gate was enabled, updates to mounted ConfigMaps were not propagated to running pods, causing pods to see stale configuration data.
112076.affected: Users running Kubernetes 1.25 with LocalStorageCapacityIsolationFSQuotaMonitoring enabled, especially workloads that rely on dynamically updated ConfigMaps.
112076.fix: The regression was fixed and the feature gate was moved back to Alpha status, restoring correct ConfigMap update behavior when the feature is enabled.
112076.impact: Clusters that had the feature enabled now receive fresh ConfigMap data without needing to restart pods, preventing configuration drift and potential application errors.

112120.problem: Legacy klog command‑line flags (e.g., --logtostderr, --stderrthreshold, --vmodule, etc.) were removed from Kubernetes binaries, leaving only -v and -vmodule supported. Scripts, tooling, or operators that relied on those flags now see unknown‑flag errors and lack expected logging behavior.
112120.affected: Any deployment that starts Kubernetes components (kubelet, kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, controller‑manager, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.) with legacy klog flags. Affects operators, CI/CD pipelines, and testing frameworks that embed those flags.
112120.fix: The binaries have been updated to drop all deprecated klog flags. Users must modify their startup commands or scripts to use only -v and -vmodule (or configure logging via environment variables) to control log verbosity.
112120.impact: Ensures a consistent, minimal logging flag set across the project and reduces maintenance burden. However, existing automation that passes removed flags will fail, requiring a quick update to avoid startup failures.

112133.problem: The deprecated `userspace` proxy mode was still available in Kubernetes, but as of this release it is no longer supported on Linux or Windows, causing kube-proxy to fail to start for clusters that still rely on that mode.
112133.affected: Any cluster that configured kube-proxy with `--proxy-mode=userspace` on Linux or Windows will be affected; workloads relying on that mode will see network failures.
112133.fix: Support for `userspace` mode has been removed. Users must configure kube-proxy to use `iptables` or `ipvs` on Linux, or `kernelspace` on Windows.
112133.impact: Clusters that were using the userspace proxy will lose pod network connectivity until they switch to a supported mode. The change finalizes a year‑long deprecation, simplifying the code base and reducing unmaintained traffic‑distribution code.

112243.problem: In Kubernetes 1.25, several rarely‑used flags for the `kubectl run` command were removed before they completed the required deprecation period, breaking scripts and workflows that still referenced those flags.
112243.affected: Anyone using the `kubectl run` command with the now‑restored flags (e.g., CI pipelines, custom scripts, and developers).
112243.fix: The missing flags have been reinstated on `kubectl run`, restoring the original command interface and ensuring the deprecation process is respected before any future removal.
112243.impact: Users and automation that relied on the previously removed flags can run `kubectl run` without errors again, preserving backward compatibility and preventing unexpected command failures.

112257.problem: The kube-scheduler ComponentConfig API versions v1beta2 and v1beta3 are being deprecated and will be removed in upcoming releases (v1.28 and v1.29 respectively). Clusters that still reference these versions will encounter errors when the versions are removed.
112257.affected: Clusters that configure the kube-scheduler via ComponentConfig using API versions v1beta2 or v1beta3.
112257.fix: Update any Scheduler ComponentConfig manifests to use a supported version (e.g., v1beta4 or later) before the removal deadlines. Adjust tooling and documentation to reference the newer API version.
112257.impact: Ensures clusters continue to start the scheduler without configuration errors. Prevents upgrade failures and the need for emergency rollbacks after the removal points.

112261.problem: kubectl run exposed several flags (--cascade, --filename, --force, --grace-period, --kustomize, --recursive, --timeout, --wait) that have no effect, causing user confusion and implying support for features that aren't implemented.
112261.affected: Anyone using the kubectl run command with the listed flags, particularly those who attempted to use --kustomize or other ignored options.
112261.fix: These flags are now deprecated and documented as ignored when set, preventing their use and signaling removal in future releases.
112261.impact: Users will no longer be misled into using ineffective flags with kubectl run, leading to clearer CLI behavior and fewer wasted troubleshooting steps.

112341.problem: The built‑in GCP and Azure authentication plugins were removed from client‑go and kubectl, causing clusters that relied on these plugins to fail authentication.
112341.affected: Any user or automation that authenticates to GKE or AKS clusters using the built‑in `gcp` or `azure` auth plugins in kubectl or client‑go.
112341.fix: The plugins are no longer shipped; users must switch to the cloud‑specific replacements (kubelogin for Azure and the GKE auth plugin for GCP) as documented.
112341.impact: Clusters accessed with GCP or Azure auth via kubectl or client‑go will need to install and configure the external plugins, otherwise API requests will be rejected. This change centralises cloud‑specific auth handling and reduces the client‑go code base.

112386.problem: The CSRDuration feature gate remained in the codebase even after the CertificateSigningRequest.Spec.ExpirationSeconds field graduated to GA and the gate became always enabled.
112386.affected: Clusters upgrading to v1.26 that still have the CSRDuration feature gate set in the apiserver configuration.
112386.fix: The CSRDuration feature gate has been removed entirely from the source, eliminating the obsolete flag and related gating logic.
112386.impact: Upgrading to v1.26 no longer requires handling the CSRDuration flag; clusters are simpler and there is no functional change for users. Any existing configuration that referenced the flag will be ignored or cause a warning.

112567.problem: The GA feature gates DefaultPodTopologySpread, NonPreemptingPriority, PodAffinityNamespaceSelector, and PreferNominatedNode were still registered in the code base, requiring users to reference them even though they have been permanently enabled.
112567.affected: Clusters upgrading from v1.24/v1.25 to v1.26 that still have the removed feature‑gate names in the scheduler’s config or custom manifests.
112567.fix: Removed the now‑redundant feature gates from kube‑scheduler. The underlying functionality remains enabled unconditionally; the flags are no longer recognized.
112567.impact: Upgrading clusters to v1.26 will no longer accept these feature‑gate names. Configurations that still list them must be cleaned up, otherwise the scheduler will reject the configuration. Otherwise there is no behavior change, simplifying the scheduler binary and configuration.

112577.problem: The feature gates ServiceLoadBalancerClass and ServiceLBNodePortControl remained in the codebase even though they had been enabled and locked as default since v1.24, leading to unnecessary configuration flags.
112577.affected: Clusters that explicitly set ServiceLoadBalancerClass or ServiceLBNodePortControl feature gates in kube-apiserver or controller-manager configurations will need to remove those flags.
112577.fix: Both feature gates have been removed from the code and documentation. Clusters no longer need to (and cannot) set these flags; the related functionality is always enabled.
112577.impact: Simplifies cluster configuration and removes the possibility of setting obsolete flags that would cause validation errors. No functional behavior changes for workloads.

112579.problem: The `PodOverhead` feature gate remained in the codebase even though the feature graduated to GA in v1.24, so clusters could still be configured with an unnecessary/unknown flag.
112579.affected: Users who had `PodOverhead` enabled or disabled via the feature-gates flag in kube-apiserver, kubelet, or other components.
112579.fix: Removed the `PodOverhead` feature gate from all components, as the functionality is now always enabled and no longer gated.
112579.impact: Clusters no longer need to set or worry about the `PodOverhead` feature gate; configuration is simpler and any stale `--feature-gates=PodOverhead=true|false` flags are no longer accepted.

112589.problem: The IndexedJob and SuspendJob feature gates remained in the codebase even after they graduated to GA and were always enabled, causing unnecessary configuration options and potential confusion for users who might try to set them.
112589.affected: Clusters upgraded to v1.26 that had custom kube-apiserver or kube-controller-manager configurations including the IndexedJob or SuspendJob feature gates. Users who attempted to enable or disable these flags will see them no longer recognized.
112589.fix: Removed the IndexedJob and SuspendJob feature gates entirely in v1.26, eliminating the stale flags from the code and default configurations.
112589.impact: Cluster administrators no longer see or can set these obsolete feature gates, simplifying upgrade paths and reducing the chance of misconfiguration. No runtime behavior changes for jobs, as the features are already permanently enabled.

112631.problem: When image garbage collection failed, the kubelet emitted an unclear log message, making it difficult for operators to diagnose the issue.
112631.affected: Operators and cluster administrators who rely on kubelet logs to debug image garbage collection failures.
112631.fix: The log message text has been rewritten to clearly describe the failure, providing better context and actionable information.
112631.impact: Improves troubleshooting and observability for node image management without altering functionality.

112643.problem: The DynamicKubeletConfig feature gate was removed from the API server, so dynamic kubelet reconfiguration can no longer be used, even by older nodes that still expect it.
112643.affected: Clusters with the DynamicKubeletConfig feature gate enabled or nodes that depend on dynamic kubelet reconfiguration.
112643.fix: The feature gate is no longer available; dynamic kubelet configuration is disabled. Clusters must stop relying on DynamicKubeletConfig and configure kubelet settings through other means.
112643.impact: Clusters that enabled DynamicKubeletConfig or older nodes attempting to use dynamic reconfiguration will lose that capability, requiring configuration changes or node upgrades. This aligns the behavior with the Kubernetes version skew policy and prevents unsupported interactions.

112652.problem: There was no built‑in metric to tell whether a Kubernetes feature gate was enabled, making it difficult for operators to observe feature state across the cluster.
112652.affected: Any cluster component that uses feature gates and exposes metrics (e.g., kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller‑manager, kubelet) – and the users who rely on observability of those flags.
112652.fix: Introduces a new `kubernetes_feature_enabled` metric that reports the enabled/disabled status of each feature gate, exposed on the standard metrics endpoint of components that support feature gates.
112652.impact: Operators can now monitor and alert on feature‑gate status via existing Prometheus tooling, improving troubleshooting and ensuring expected configurations are in place.

112679.problem: The apiserver_request_slo_duration_seconds metric name conflates Service Level Objectives (SLO) with Service Level Indicators (SLI), causing confusion for users monitoring API server latency.
112679.affected: Any cluster that scrapes or queries the apiserver_request_slo_duration_seconds metric (e.g., monitoring dashboards, alerting rules) will need to update to the new metric name.
112679.fix: The metric is deprecated in v1.27 and replaced by apiserver_request_sli_duration_seconds, aligning the naming with other SLI-specific metrics and clarifying its purpose.
112679.impact: Monitoring setups must migrate to the new metric name, preventing misinterpretation of latency data and improving consistency across observability tools.

112690.problem: There was no built‑in metric to show whether each active feature gate was enabled, making it hard for operators to observe and alert on feature‑gate state across the cluster.
112690.affected: All clusters that run components with feature gates and rely on metrics for monitoring (e.g., kube‑apiserver, kube‑scheduler, kube‑controller‑manager, kubelet, kube‑proxy, etc.).
112690.fix: Introduces the `kubernetes_feature_enabled` metric series, which emits a boolean value for every active feature gate per component, allowing Prometheus (or other metric backends) to report the enabled state.
112690.impact: Improves cluster observability and debugging by letting users monitor feature‑gate status, set alerts, and verify configurations without inspecting component logs or configs directly.

112748.problem: The ServerSideApply feature gate could be disabled even though ServerSideApply has reached GA, causing potential confusion and inconsistent behavior for users who rely on the feature being always available.
112748.affected: Any cluster using the kube-apiserver where the ServerSideApply feature gate could be manually set to false; users who previously relied on being able to disable the feature are affected.
112748.fix: The ServerSideApply feature gate is now locked to true in the code, ensuring the feature is permanently enabled and cannot be turned off.
112748.impact: All clusters will have ServerSideApply permanently enabled, simplifying configuration, preventing accidental disabling, and ensuring consistent server‑side apply behavior across all workloads.

112806.problem: The conformance test suite required Service session affinity timeout behavior, but real-world network plugin implementations vary, making the test unreliable and causing false negatives.
112806.affected: Developers and CI systems that run Kubernetes conformance tests for network plugins; downstream projects that depended on the removed session‑affinity timeout test.
112806.fix: The Service session affinity timeout tests have been removed from the required Kubernetes network plugin conformance suite. Future releases will add new, more representative conformance tests for network plugins.
112806.impact: Reduces false test failures for plugin developers and CI pipelines, and paves the way for better conformance criteria that reflect actual implementation diversity.

112884.problem: Kubernetes lacked a dedicated endpoint for exposing Service Level Indicator (SLI) metrics per control‑plane component, preventing operators from easily collecting component‑level health metrics.
112884.affected: Clusters that need fine‑grained observability of control‑plane components (apiserver, controller‑manager, scheduler, kubelet, etc.).
112884.fix: Introduces the `ComponentSLIs` alpha feature‑gate, which when enabled adds a new metrics endpoint that publishes per‑component SLI metrics.
112884.impact: Operators can now scrape component‑specific SLI metrics for monitoring, alerting, and capacity planning, improving observability of control‑plane health.

112924.problem: Windows Server 20H2 container image flavors were still being built and published, but they are no longer supported, leading to potential confusion and wasted storage for users expecting those images to be available.
112924.affected: Clusters running Windows nodes that reference the deprecated 20H2 image flavors.
112924.fix: The release removes all Windows Server 20H2 image variants from the Kubernetes container image set, ensuring only supported Windows versions are built and published.
